page: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 64 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Built on the Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture clocked at 3.0 GHz, each vCPU corresponds directly to a physical core with one thread per core. The instance includes 1288 GB of local SSD temporary storage and supports premium storage attachments. It does not include hardware GPU acceleration or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent middle-tier throughput across multi-threaded operations, reflecting the density of 32 physical cores. In stress-ng testing, multi-core performance reached 57,238.05, while Clang software compilation registered a score of 25,849.0. Memory bandwidth delivers 143.96 GB/sec for large un-cached reads and 69.76 GB/sec for writes. Single-core performance is more modest, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1033.0 and reduced single-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput. Large language model inference on 70B parameter models remains limited due to memory capacity and lack of hardware accelerators.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the Neoverse-N1 platform provides cost-effective compute scale for multi-threaded workloads compared to traditional x86 architecture. The bundled 1288 GB local SSD adds high-speed scratch space without extra storage volume fees. However, the 2 GB per core allocation requires monitoring for memory-hungry services.

This instance suits multi-threaded scale-out tasks such as static web serving, containerized microservices, distributed build systems, and intermediate data transformation where CPU parallelism outweighs single-thread clock speed requirements.
description: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v5 is an ARM-based instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs powered by the Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture at 3.0 GHz, matched with 64 GB of memory and a bundled 1288 GB local SSD. With one thread per physical core, the instance exhibits reliable parallel computing throughput, achieving a stress-ng multi-core result of 57,238.05 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12,092.0. Single-core processing metrics and memory-intensive tasks face constraints due to modest per-thread performance and a lean 2 GB memory-per-core ratio. The absence of GPU acceleration limits heavy machine learning workloads, but the platform offers qualitative compute efficiency for highly parallelized applications. Azure D32plds_v5 fits multi-threaded workloads, including container clusters, Clang build environments, batch data processing pipelines, and web servers requiring fast local scratch storage.
